clue.text: Happening singleton in part of West London

indicators.note: in places the single letter within the name of the London district

parts.note: Acton is a district of West London
a singleton is a lone one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone single is out and about in a corner of West London, where things are going on.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of West London.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is something taking place, an event or occurrence, as in 'where the action is'.

clue.text: Loco? Calm down!

parts.note: the clue word is what you get when the word cool is set off, that is scrambled: an anagram of COOL

explanation.surface: Someone tells a person acting crazily to settle down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: COOL, with 'off' as an anagram signal, gives LOCO, the word printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool off is to lose one's anger or excitement, an idiom for calming down.

clue.text: Unopened web publication

indicators.note: unopened means the word loses its first letter, its opening

parts.note: a tissue is a web, as in a tissue of lies

explanation.surface: An online magazine or post that nobody has opened yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unopened' removes the T from TISSUE; 'web' looks like the internet but means a woven fabric or network.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a single edition of a magazine or periodical that is published.

clue.text: Grandee, one retaining aura somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: retaining means holding something within, so the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: a nob is a toff or grandee
an air is an aura or atmosphere about someone
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grand nobleman with a certain presence, pictured somewhere on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' puts the aura word inside after the first letter of the grandee word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, so it is a place in Africa.

clue.text: Dancing monkey maybe joining tap group

indicators.note: joining here means coming in among, so the animal goes inside the other letters

parts.note: C marks the cold tap
a ring is a group or gang
a monkey is an example of an ape, loosely

explanation.surface: A dancing monkey teams up with a tap-dance troupe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tap' looks like tap dancing but is a water tap, labelled C for cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Capering is skipping and leaping about playfully, a kind of frisky dancing.

clue.text: Traditional values of pious community — disciplinarians at centre lay it on liberally

parts.note: a convent is a religious community of nuns

indicators.note: at centre picks the single middle letter of the long word
liberally means freely, so the letters are mixed up without restraint

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Strict rule-enforcers in a devout community lay on traditional values heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at centre' takes I, the eighth of fifteen letters; 'liberally' mixes it with the three printed words into IONALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventionality is adherence to accepted customs and norms, which is to say traditional values.

clue.text: Story could be cut shorter?

indicators.note: shorter means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
able means could, capable of being

explanation.surface: A wry note that a story would benefit from editing down.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue also reads as a whole: something 'pare-able' could be cut, and dropping a letter makes it shorter.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, a kind of story told to teach a lesson.

clue.text: Bizarre glories in spiritual traditions

indicators.note: bizarre means strange or odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Strange glories found within spiritual traditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Religions are systems of faith and worship, which are spiritual traditions.

clue.text: Present, present, absent

parts.note: present in time: now, at this moment
present in place: here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A roll call answer that contradicts itself: present, present, absent.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'present's take different senses, time and place.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is nowhere it is not in any place, so absent or missing.

clue.text: To follow evening meal hosts start to smoke hash …

indicators.note: hosts means holds as guest, so the single letter sits within the other letters

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them
dinner is the evening meal

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: After dinner the hosts light up and smoke some cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' looks like the drug, but it means a mess, as in making a hash of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's dinner is British slang for a muddle, which is what making a hash of something produces.

clue.text: … briefly contemplate turning lecherous …

indicators.note: turning means the word is read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to dwell on something is to contemplate it

explanation.surface: Someone stops to consider a moment and becomes lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: DWELL less its last letter is DWEL, which 'turning' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means crude and lustful in a sexual way, a close synonym of lecherous.

clue.text: … share a little melancholy…

parts.note: to dole out is to share or hand out portions
some means a little, an amount

explanation.surface: Someone shares a touch of sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolesome is an old word for doleful or gloomy, sharing the root of dolour, sorrow.

clue.text: … budge off around midnight, wired

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters encircle the middle letter
off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the middle of the word night is its letter G

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off around midnight, all wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wired' looks like jittery, but means fitted with listening devices.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugged room is wired with hidden microphones, so wired here means fitted for eavesdropping.

clue.text: Warning cry let off within solitary confinement

parts.note: to fire is to let off a gun
within means in
the hole is prison slang for a solitary confinement cell

explanation.surface: A prisoner in solitary lets out a warning shout.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is shouted to warn that an explosive is about to be detonated.

clue.text: Canine treatment too carnal to be recreated

indicators.note: to be recreated means made again in a new form, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A dog's treatment considered too lustful to be staged again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, but it is the pointed tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: This dental procedure clears infected pulp from a tooth, such as a canine.

clue.text: Mixer and drop of rosso drunk outside church

indicators.note: outside means the scrambled letters surround the church letters
drunk means intoxicated, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sociable type downs a drop of red wine outside church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' looks like a sociable person; rosso is Italian red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A food processor is a kitchen machine that blends and chops, a type of mixer.

clue.text: Rosy-cheeked as illness cast off

parts.note: flu is influenza, an illness
to shed is to cast off

explanation.surface: Someone looks pink in the face as they shake off an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Flushed means having a reddened face, which is what being rosy in the cheeks describes.

clue.text: By heart disturbance one demonstrates love for Georgia or Jordan perhaps

definitions.text: one demonstrates love for Georgia or Jordan perhaps

parts.note: to know something off pat is to know it by heart
a riot is a public disturbance

explanation.surface: A heart flutter in someone who shows love for a person named Georgia or Jordan.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia and Jordan look like people's names, but they are countries.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves and defends their country, and Georgia and Jordan are examples of countries.

clue.text: Accessory making money but keeping right to withhold name

indicators.note: keeping means taking in a letter in place of another
to withhold means to hold back a letter, removing it

parts.note: earning is making money

explanation.surface: A jewellery accessory that earns money while dodging naming anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In EARNING, R is kept in place of the N withheld.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is a piece of jewellery worn on the ear, a fashion accessory.

clue.text: Likely martyr and partner turning rebels

indicators.note: turning means the combined letters read in reverse, upwards in this down entry

parts.note: ST stands for saint, and saints are often martyrs
a lover is a partner

explanation.surface: A would-be martyr and their companion become rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolts as a verb means rises up against authority, which is what someone who rebels does.

clue.text: Sweet wine's pronounced aroma — flipping cheers!

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the scent word is given by its sound

parts.note: musk is a strong aroma

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the thank-you word reads backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A sweet wine with a strong scent, toasted with an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like an exasperated intensifier, but it reverses TA (British slang for thanks).
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a sweet dessert wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: Coarse sailor is capsized in storm

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: in means placed within the rage word

parts.note: to rave is to storm or rage

indicators.note: capsized means overturned, so the little word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A rough-and-ready sailor overturned in a storm at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive means rough and harsh in texture, like sandpaper, so coarse.

clue.text: Rash is briefly on top of head

indicators.note: on top of means placed above in this down entry

parts.note: is shortened to 's
the pate is the top of the head

explanation.surface: A skin rash appearing on top of someone's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint, but means a sudden outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood of things, like a rash of burglaries.

clue.text: Avoid attention during parade

definitions.meaning: the clipped drill command 'Attention!' barked on the parade ground

explanation.surface: Steering clear of standing to attention on parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Shun means keep away from, and 'shun is the shortened military command to stand to attention.

clue.text: Unique car returned, albeit damaged

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the car's name reads backwards

parts.note: the Mini is a classic small car

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind car sent back to the dealer, though it was damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimitable means impossible to copy, so unique and without equal.

clue.text: Wedding vow: glad at heart attempt to create devotion

parts.note: I do is the vow said at a wedding

indicators.note: at heart takes the middle letters of the word

parts.note: a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A happy couple's wedding vow as an attempt to build devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is worship of idols, and loosely any excessive devotion to someone.

clue.text: Mineral content of champagne is slight

indicators.note: content of means the letters held inside these words

explanation.surface: The mineral content of a champagne is only small.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' sounds like a nutrition label, but it means what the words hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock, loosely called a mineral in crosswords.
